line: Labels used to look past me, now they trying to remake me Grab a fat nigga out the trenches and replace me Tryna duplicate me, can’t be
vault_lines: Labels used to look past me, now they trying to remake me
meaning:
This appears to be shot at North Carolina artist Morray, who started gaining popularity in 2020 with his hit song “Quicksand.” Shortly after signing to Interscope Records, Morray released another single entitled “Trenches,” which has since been remixed with Polo G.

A signee of Alamo Records, Rod is upset that labels ignored him in the past but now try to ‘replace’ or replicate his success with similar artists. Morray himself has commented on the fact that fans online often compare him to Rod due to the amount of singing on both of their records.

Shortly following the release of SoulFly (Deluxe), there appeared to be some tension between Rod and Morray over a potential feature spot on “In My Blood,” a posthumous release from the artist MO3. MO3’s manager explained that the track was made for Rod’s appearance, but Morray replaced him because he was “more genuine.”
